faq.title: FAQ
faq.answer.upload:
No. JexFold processes images locally on your device. Files are not sent to a server and never leave your computer.

In the web version, conversion runs directly in your browser using WebAssembly. After the app loads, processing can work offline.
faq.question.why: Why convert JPEG to JPEG XL?
faq.answer.why:
JPEG XL can store existing JPEG files more efficiently.

JexFold uses reversible JPEG → JXL recompression: the image is not re-encoded with another quality loss, and the original JPEG can be restored bit-for-bit.

As a result, JXL usually takes up less space while the original JPEG remains fully recoverable.

The savings depend on the individual file.
faq.answer.quality:
No. For JPEG, JexFold uses reversible JPEG XL recompression.

After conversion, the app restores a JPEG from the resulting JXL and compares it with the original file byte by byte. A file is considered successfully converted only when they match completely.

This preserves not only the image, but also the ability to restore the original JPEG in its initial form.
faq.question.jpeg: Why not just keep photos as JPEG?
faq.answer.jpeg:
You can. JPEG remains a highly compatible format, and JexFold does not require you to move your archive to JXL.

JPEG XL is most useful for large collections: even a moderate reduction in each file can noticeably reduce the total size of an archive, backups, and cloud storage.

JexFold lets you get those savings without irreversibly changing the original JPEGs.
